conflicts.point: Whether structural unbundling of vertically integrated artificial intelligence firms is necessary to ensure adequate safety oversight or merely cements incumbent compliance moats.

positions.stance: Structural unbundling is necessary to decouple infrastructure ownership from model deployment, preventing safety oversight from remaining subordinate to commercial speed.
Mandatory structural unbundling destroys the tight technical integration between custom silicon and massive data centers required to fund and train frontier AI models.
Structural separation creates complex compliance bureaucracies that burden small entrants while cementing incumbent dominance through legal tollbooths.

verdicts.conflict: Whether structural unbundling of vertically integrated artificial intelligence firms is necessary to ensure adequate safety oversight or merely cements incumbent compliance moats.
verdicts.rationale: Safetyists provide concrete evidence that closed architectures block thirty-day workload portability, while skeptics correctly note that judicial breakups create compliance bureaucracies that burden independent entrants. Neither position demonstrates that its preferred remedy avoids creating new market distortions.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Longitudinal compliance data from regulated technology sectors demonstrating whether structural separation successfully lowers barriers to entry for smaller firms over a five-year period.
